subtitle: Watch the shape ahead of the next enemy

body: TxK is Llamasoft's PlayStation Vita arcade shooter, first released in North America on 11 February 2014. Designed by Jeff Minter, it places the player at the edge of geometric playfields while enemies travel along their lanes towards the rim. Movement around that boundary and fire directed into the approaching formations create a clear central task. The changing shapes and visual effects give the action a more intense character, but success begins with reading the lanes. A threat has to be recognised early enough to reach the correct position before it arrives.

Additional abilities expand the player's responses as a run continues, allowing the game to develop beyond the initial movement and firing pattern. An option removes those power-ups for a different kind of challenge. The player balances attention to the immediate lane with awareness of enemies elsewhere on the shape, deciding when to remain in place and when to move around the rim. The restricted path makes those decisions readable. Even when the display becomes busy, the next useful action depends on understanding which section of the boundary is about to become dangerous.

TxK received strong reviews, with its compact arcade design finding a natural home on the Vita. Planned releases for other platforms did not proceed after Atari raised legal objections over similarities to Tempest 2000. That history left the original handheld release unusually isolated despite its favourable reception. The game belongs to Minter's long interest in combining precise shooting with intense audiovisual patterns. Its appeal comes from keeping those layers connected: the spectacle surrounds a task the player can understand immediately, then continues testing how accurately that understanding can be maintained as the shapes and threats change.
